items.title: [Bug]: Discord adapter creates zombie websocket connection on reconnect, causing double responses

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Description

When the gateway restarts (or the Discord adapter reconnects), `DiscordAdapter.connect()` creates a new `commands.Bot` client but never closes the old one. Discord doesn't immediately terminate the old websocket, leaving two live connections for a window of time. Both connections receive every incoming message, resulting in two separate agent turns being spawned — each generating a different response.

## Symptoms

- Every Discord message triggers two responses with different wording (not a duplicate of the same response)
- When `auto_thread` is enabled: one response appears in the auto-created thread (correct), a second response appears directly in the parent channel (incorrect)
- Gateway log shows the same message arriving twice ~400ms apart:
  ```
  inbound message: platform=discord user=X chat=Y msg='hello'
  inbound message: platform=discord user=X chat=Y msg='hello'   ← ~400ms later
  ```
- Only one gateway process is running (`ps aux` confirms)
- `MessageDeduplicator` exists and is correctly placed, but fails due to the race condition between two concurrent websocket deliveries

## Root Cause

In `gateway/platforms/discord.py`, `connect()` unconditionally creates a new `commands.Bot` instance:

```python
self._client = commands.Bot(
    command_prefix="!",
    intents=intents,
    ...
)
```

When `connect()` is called a second time (e.g. during reconnect in `run.py` line ~2848), the old `self._client` is orphaned — still connected to Discord's gateway — while the new client also connects. Both are alive simultaneously and both fire `on_message` for every event.

The `MessageDeduplicator` (per-adapter instance) cannot prevent duplicates because both websockets deliver the event independently, and the two `on_message` coroutines may check `is_duplicate` before either has marked the ID as seen (race condition).

## Fix

Before creating the new `Bot` instance in `connect()`, close and await the old client if one exists:

```python
# Add before: self._client = commands.Bot(...)
if self._client and not self._client.is_closed():
    await self._client.close()
    self._client = None
self._ready_event.clear()
```

This ensures only one Discord websocket connection is ever active for the adapter at any time.

## Environment

- Hermes gateway running in Docker container
- Discord platform adapter
- `auto_thread: true` in config (makes the symptom very visible — thread response + channel response)
- Triggered by any gateway restart or reconnect cycle

## Workaround

Avoid gateway restarts. The zombie connection eventually times out on its own (~minutes), after which responses return to normal until the next restart.

items.title: TUI Shift+Enter submits instead of newline when terminal sends LF

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

In the modern Hermes TUI, some terminal stacks can distinguish plain Enter from Shift+Enter/Ctrl+J only by the raw byte received:

- plain Enter sends CR (`\r`, byte `13`)
- Shift+Enter / Ctrl+J sends LF (`\n`, byte `10`)

Hermes already has TUI input logic that can treat raw LF as “insert newline”, but the lower-level `hermes-ink` key parser clears `keypress.raw` for both CR and LF when it normalizes them to `key.return`. As a result, `TextInput` cannot see `event.keypress.raw === '\n'`, so LF falls through as a normal return/submit instead of multiline input.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a terminal stack where raw-mode input reports:
   - Enter → `13` / `\r`
   - Shift+Enter → `10` / `\n`
2. Start the modern TUI: `hermes --tui`
3. Type text in the composer.
4. Press Shift+Enter.

## Expected Behavior

Shift+Enter inserts a newline in the current draft while plain Enter submits.

## Actual Behavior

Shift+Enter is normalized as `return` with no raw byte preserved, so it submits like plain Enter.

## Environment

Observed on macOS terminal stack using Warp/tmux over SSH, where raw-mode byte testing confirms Enter and Shift+Enter arrive as distinct CR/LF bytes.

## Proposed Fix

Preserve `keypress.raw` for CR/LF in `ui-tui/packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/parse-keypress.ts` so `ui-tui/src/components/textInput.tsx` can distinguish LF and insert a newline.

items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

When using reasoning models (DeepSeek V4, Sonnet 4.6, etc.) in the TUI, tool calls are frequently interleaved with thinking blocks: the model thinks, calls a tool, thinks about the result, calls another tool, and so on. The actual chronological order carries important signal — you can see what the model was reasoning about *before* deciding on each specific tool call.

Currently the TUI groups everything by type:

```
┌─ Thinking ──────────────┐
│ (all thinking blocks    │
│  concatenated together) │
└─────────────────────────┘
┌─ Tool calls ────────────┐
│ ● Search Files          │
│ ● Read File             │
│ ● Write File            │
└─────────────────────────┘
```

This makes it hard to trace which thinking led to which tool call, especially for multi-step reasoning workflows.

## Proposed Solution

A config option (e.g. `display.interleave_thinking`, default `false`) that renders thinking blocks and tool calls in their actual chronological sequence:

```
┌─ Thinking ──────┐
│ (first block)   │
└─────────────────┘
  ● Search Files
┌─ Thinking ──────┐
│ (second block)  │
└─────────────────┘
  ● Read File
┌─ Thinking ──────┐
│ (third block)   │
└─────────────────┘
  ● Write File
```

Implementation notes:
- The `segmentMessages` array in `turnController.ts` already preserves chronological order of segments
- The backend currently concatenates all reasoning blocks into one string — this would need to pass reasoning as a list of `{text, toolCall}` timeline entries instead
- The `ToolTrail` component (`ui-tui/src/components/thinking.tsx`) would render a timeline rather than two hardcoded grouped panels

## Alternatives Considered

- **Slash command** (`/details interleave`): more discoverable but transient; config key persists across sessions
- **Always interleaved (no config)**: would break the compact grouped view that works well for simple turns with 1-2 tool calls; opt-in via config is lower risk
- **CLI verbose mode improvement**: could also benefit, but TUI is the primary surface for this change

## Feature Type

- CLI improvement

## Scope

- Medium (few files, < 300 lines): backend reasoning assembly + TUI ToolTrail rendering

items.title: [Bug]: auth.json credential cache ignores .env changes — stale key persists

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug Description

When `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (or other env-seeded credentials) is updated in `~/.hermes/.env`, the cached credential in `auth.json` (`credential_pool.openrouter`) is **not invalidated**. Hermes continues using the old cached key, resulting in silent 401 errors.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=test-key-fresh` in `~/.hermes/.env` and start Hermes
2. Update `~/.hermes/.env` with a valid key (e.g. `sk-or-...b854`)
3. Restart Hermes gateway
4. Try to use an OpenRouter model → HTTP 401 "Missing Authentication header"
5. Check `auth.json` → credential still has `access_token: "test-key-fresh"`

## Root Cause

The credential pool seeds from env vars via `_seed_from_env()` in `agent/credential_pool.py`. It calls `get_env_value()` which checks `os.environ` FIRST, then falls back to `~/.hermes/.env`:

```python
def get_env_value(key: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Get a value from ~/.hermes/.env or environment."""
    if key in os.environ:
        return os.environ[key]     # <-- takes priority over .env!
    env_vars = load_env()
    return env_vars.get(key)
```

If any parent process (e.g. Codex CLI, test script) has exported `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=test-key-fresh`, that stale value shadows the actual key in `.env`. The credential pool then caches this stale value in `auth.json` and never re-reads `.env`.

The fix should ensure that `~/.hermes/.env` is the authoritative source for Hermes config, with `os.environ` only as a secondary fallback — not the override.

## Expected Behavior

- Updating a key in `~/.hermes/.env` + restarting Hermes should use the new key
- `auth.json` cache should reflect the `.env` file content, not stale `os.environ` values from parent shell processes

## Actual Behavior

- `auth.json` retains a snapshot of whichever value was in `os.environ` at the time of first load
- Changing `.env` does not update the cached credential
- Users get 401 errors with no indication that the cache is stale

## Environment

- Hermes v0.12.0 (2026.4.30)
- macOS (local CLI)
- Tested with OpenRouter provider

## Diagnostic Command

```bash
python3 -c "
import json
a = json.load(open(\"/Users/xuefusong/.hermes/auth.json\"))
c = a[\"credential_pool\"][\"openrouter\"][0]
print(f\"Cached key: {c[\"access_token\"]}\")
print(f\"Source: {c[\"source\"]}\")
print(f\"Status: {c.get(\"last_status\")}\")
import os
print(f\"Env var: {os.environ.get(\"OPENROUTER_API_KEY\", \"(not set)\")[:20]}...\")
" 2>&1
```

items.title: [Bug]: TUI eagerly persists empty sessions to DB — ghost sessions clutter /resume
items.body:
[Bug]: TUI eagerly persists sessions to DB before any message is sent — empty ghost sessions clutter /resume

## Bug Description

When starting `hermes --tui` and immediately quitting (Ctrl+C or /quit) without sending any message, an empty session row is created in `state.db` that appears in `/resume`. The same happens with `/new` — each invocation creates a session row even if no message is ever sent.

CLI (`hermes`) does NOT have this problem: sessions are lazily persisted on first message via `_flush_messages_to_session_db() → ensure_session()`. If you quit CLI without sending a message, the in-memory session_id never reaches the DB.

On the user's install, this has produced **24 empty TUI sessions** (message_count=0, ended_at=NULL) out of 52 total TUI sessions — ~46% are noise.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `hermes --tui`
2. Wait for the TUI to render (a few seconds for agent build to complete)
3. Press Ctrl+C or type `/quit` — do NOT send any message
4. Repeat 2–3 more times
5. Run `hermes sessions list` or `/resume` in TUI — observe empty sessions
6. Alternatively, inspect the DB:
```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM sessions WHERE source='tui' AND message_count=0 AND ended_at IS NULL;
```

## Expected Behavior

A session should only be persisted to the DB when it has actual content (at least one user message). Quitting without sending a message should leave no trace in /resume.

Alternatively, if eager session creation is retained for technical reasons, `end_session()` must be called on quit to mark the session as closed (`ended_at` set, `end_reason` set), so the /resume picker can filter it out.

## Actual Behavior

TUI sessions are created eagerly during `session.create` → `_start_agent_build()` at:

- **`tui_gateway/server.py` line 544**: `db.create_session(key, source="tui", model=_resolve_model())`

This is called via a 50ms deferred timer (line 1999–2003), so it reliably fires before the user can quit. Once created, the session row remains with `ended_at=NULL` indefinitely because:

1. **No `end_session()` call exists anywhere in `tui_gateway/`** — verified by searching the entire directory
2. `session.close` handler (line 2421) calls `_finalize_session()` (line 283) which only commits memory + fires hooks — it does NOT call `db.end_session()`
3. `_shutdown_sessions()` (atexit handler, line 306) also only calls `_finalize_session()`, no `end_session()`

By contrast, CLI properly ends sessions:
- `cli.py` line 4927: `end_session(old_session_id, "new_session")` on `/new`
- `cli.py` line 11520: `end_session(self.agent.session_id, "cli_close")` on quit

### Confirmed: `/new` has the same problem

`/new` in TUI calls `newSession()` → `session.create` RPC → same `db.create_session()` path. Each `/new` without sending a message creates another ghost session.

## Root Cause

Two separate gaps in TUI session lifecycle:

1. **Eager DB creation**: `_start_agent_build()` writes to DB before any user input. Fix: delay `db.create_session()` until first message (mirror CLI's lazy approach), or wrap it in a `finally` that calls `end_session` if the session was never used.

2. **Missing `end_session` on close**: `session.close` and `_shutdown_sessions` never call `db.end_session()`. Fix: add `db.end_session(key, "tui_close")` to `_finalize_session()` or the close handler.

## Environment

- Hermes source: `tui_gateway/server.py`, current `main` (confirmed via code inspection)
- OS: WSL2 / Linux
- Impact: all TUI users, every `hermes --tui` launch accumulates noise in /resume

## Related

- #12029 — broader session leak issue covering gateway/cli/cron; this is a concrete sub-case with specific code locations

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Bug Description

Mattermost top-level channel posts currently enter the gateway with `source.thread_id = None`. Because Hermes session keys include `thread_id`, all new top-level posts in the same Mattermost channel collapse into the same session key.

That means the adapter active-session guard treats separate Mattermost root threads as one conversation. If one thread is processing, a second root-thread request in the same channel is queued/interrupted instead of running concurrently.

## Expected Behavior

Each Mattermost root post that Hermes replies to as a thread should become its own gateway session/thread context, so multiple Mattermost threaded conversations in the same channel can process at the same time.

Follow-up replies inside an existing Mattermost thread should continue to use the Mattermost `root_id` and therefore remain in that same Hermes session.

## Actual Behavior

Separate Mattermost root posts in one channel share one session key because they have no inbound `thread_id`. Only one threaded conversation can process at a time.

Progress/status/media follow-up sends can also miss the Mattermost root unless `metadata.thread_id` is respected by the Mattermost adapter.

## Root Cause

- `gateway/platforms/mattermost.py` sets `thread_id = post.get("root_id") or None`.
- For root posts, `root_id` is empty, so `thread_id` is `None`.
- `gateway.session.build_session_key()` therefore keys by channel only.
- The base adapter active-session guard sees all root posts in the same channel as one active session.

## Proposed Fix

For Mattermost non-DM top-level channel/group posts:

- Set inbound `source.thread_id` to `post.id` when `root_id` is absent.
- Keep replies inside existing Mattermost threads keyed by `root_id`.
- Ensure outbound Mattermost sends prefer `metadata.thread_id` over `reply_to` when setting `root_id`, so progress/status/media sends stay in the correct thread.
- Keep DM behavior unchanged unless Mattermost supplies `root_id`.

## Verification

Regression tests should cover:

- Top-level Mattermost root posts get `source.thread_id = post.id`.
- Two top-level root posts in the same channel produce distinct `build_session_key()` values.
- Two such posts start separate background processing tasks and do not enter `_pending_messages`.
- Mattermost media/progress/status sends with only `metadata.thread_id` route to the correct `root_id`.

## Feature Description

The `clarify` tool works great in CLI/TUI mode but returns "not available in this execution context" on Telegram and other messaging platforms. The root cause is that `gateway/run.py` never passes a `clarify_callback` to `AIAgent()`.

## Motivation

The `clarify` tool lets the agent ask structured multiple-choice questions -- exactly the kind of interaction that's valuable on messaging platforms where quick tap-to-respond beats typing. Currently, users on Telegram have to manually type answers to agent questions, which is slow and friction-prone.

## Proposed Solution

The Telegram adapter already has all the necessary infrastructure:

- `send_approval_prompt_with_buttons()` -- sends `InlineKeyboardMarkup` with tappable buttons
- `_handle_inline_keyboard_callback()` -- processes button taps and resolves callbacks

What's missing: a `_clarify_callback` method on the gateway runner (or platform adapter) that:

1. Sends the question + choices as inline keyboard buttons (one button per choice, plus "Other / Skip")
2. Waits for the user's button tap or text reply
3. Returns the selected choice to the agent

Then pass it when constructing `AIAgent()` in `gateway/run.py`:

```
agent = AIAgent(
    ...
    clarify_callback=self._clarify_callback,
)
```

The existing `send_approval_prompt_with_buttons()` with its `ea:` callback_data prefix and the `_handle_inline_keyboard_callback` handler provide a proven pattern that could be adapted for `ca:` (clarify) callbacks.

## Current Workaround

None. The tool is simply unavailable on messaging platforms.

items.title: TUI (--tui): Copy/paste from terminal does not work on GNOME Terminal
items.body:
## Bug Description

When launching Hermes Agent with `hermes --tui` from a Linux terminal, copy and paste from the TUI to the system clipboard does not work.

This is a **GNOME Terminal 3.60.0 + VTE 0.84.0** issue — GNOME Terminal does not implement OSC52 clipboard sequences, which is the primary clipboard mechanism the TUI relies on.

---

## Environment

- **Terminal**: GNOME Terminal 3.60.0 (VTE 0.84.0 +BIDI +GNUTLS +ICU +SYSTEMD)
- **Platform**: Linux (Fedora 44, x86_64)
- **Display Server**: Wayland (`WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0`)
- **TERM**: xterm-256color
- **Invocation**: `hermes --tui` from CLI

---

## Expected Behavior

The TUI uses OSC52 (Operating System Command 52) to read from and write to the system clipboard:

- **Copy from TUI**: When text is selected and copied, the TUI writes to the system clipboard via OSC52.
- **Paste to TUI**: When the user pastes, the TUI reads from the system clipboard via OSC52.

On terminals that support OSC52 (xterm, iTerm2, Alacritty, Kitty, tmux with passthrough enabled), this works correctly.

---

## Actual Behavior

- **Copy**: OSC52 write is sent, but GNOME Terminal ignores it — text is never copied to the system clipboard.
- **Paste**: OSC52 read query is sent, but GNOME Terminal does not respond with clipboard contents, so paste returns null/empty.

The TUI has native fallback tools available:
- **wl-paste** is installed and works correctly (`wl-paste --type text` returns clipboard content).
- `clipboard.ts` tries `xclip` first on Linux X11, then `wl-paste` for Wayland — but the OSC52 path is attempted first and fails silently on GNOME Terminal.

---

## Relevant Code

- `ui-tui/src/lib/osc52.ts` — OSC52 clipboard read/write
- `ui-tui/src/lib/clipboard.ts` — fallback chain (pbpaste → powershell → wl-paste → xclip)
- `ui-tui/src/components/textInput.tsx` — paste handling
- `ui-tui/src/lib/platform.ts` — platform/terminal detection
- `tui_gateway/server.py` — `clipboard.paste` RPC method

---

## Proposed Fix

Detect GNOME Terminal via `GNOME_TERMINAL_SERVICE` or `VTE_VERSION` environment variables, and skip OSC52 in favor of native clipboard tools:

items.title: Plugin-added tools are dropped when they target an existing built-in toolset

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description
When a plugin registers a tool into an existing built-in toolset, the tool can exist in the live registry but still be missing from session tool definitions.

Observed case:
- plugin: `image_advanced`
- tool: `image_generate_advanced`
- target toolset: `image_gen`

The plugin was enabled and loaded successfully, and the tool was present in the live registry under `image_gen`, but new sessions exposed only `image_generate` and not `image_generate_advanced`.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Enable the bundled standalone plugin `image_advanced`.
2. Start a fresh Hermes session with `image_gen` enabled.
3. Verify these three layers:
   - `registry.get_tool_names_for_toolset('image_gen')`
   - `toolsets.resolve_toolset('image_gen')`
   - `model_tools.get_tool_definitions(enabled_toolsets=['image_gen'])`
4. Observe that the registry layer includes `image_generate_advanced`, while resolved toolsets and final tool definitions do not.

## Expected Behavior
If a plugin registers a tool into an existing built-in toolset, that tool should be included in:
- `get_toolset(...)`
- `resolve_toolset(...)`
- final session tool definitions

## Actual Behavior
Built-in toolsets are returned directly from static `TOOLSETS`, so plugin-added tools for that same toolset are dropped during resolution.

Example from a real run:
- `registry.get_tool_names_for_toolset('image_gen')` -> `['image_generate', 'image_generate_advanced']`
- `resolve_toolset('image_gen')` -> `['image_generate']`
- `get_tool_definitions(enabled_toolsets=['image_gen'])` -> only `image_generate`

## Root Cause
`toolsets.get_toolset(name)` returns the static built-in definition immediately when `name in TOOLSETS`.
That means it never merges in live registry membership for plugin-added tools targeting the same toolset.

So the system correctly loads the plugin and registers the tool, but the toolset resolver silently discards it.

## Minimal Fix
For built-in toolsets, merge:
- static `TOOLSETS[name]['tools']`
- live `registry.get_tool_names_for_toolset(name)`

before returning the toolset definition.

## Notes
I verified a local patch that makes `get_toolset('image_gen')`, `resolve_toolset('image_gen')`, and `get_tool_definitions(enabled_toolsets=['image_gen'])` all include both tools.

I also added a regression test covering the case where a plugin adds a tool to an existing built-in toolset.

items.title: feat(teams): migrate plugin to microsoft-teams-apps 2.0.0 stable API

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Context

[microsoft-teams-apps 2.0.0 stable](https://pypi.org/project/microsoft-teams-apps/2.0.0/) was released on 2026-04-30 and brings a number of API changes from the \`2.0.0a*\` alpha series the Teams plugin currently targets.

The plugin is partway migrated already — commit [\`624057fc\`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/624057fce6e676df008e55f35f1219ad3b367474) (\`feat(teams): set User-Agent to Hermes via 2.0.0 client option\`) added the new \`client=ClientOptions(...)\` kwarg to the \`App()\` constructor, but the rest of the constructor still uses the alpha-style kwargs (\`client_id=, client_secret=, tenant_id=, http_server_adapter=\`) and the broader API surface (auth, validators, etc.) hasn't been swept yet.

## Why this matters

Pinning to \`microsoft-teams-apps==2.0.0a78\` to keep the plugin working has a few sharp edges that downstream operators are hitting:

### 1. The alpha series has bugs that 2.0.0 stable fixes

In \`2.0.0a78\` (and we believe most of the alpha series), \`microsoft_teams.apps.auth.token_validator.is_allowed_service_url()\` reads \`cloud.allowed_service_urls\`, but the \`CloudEnvironment\` dataclass in \`microsoft_teams.api.auth.cloud_environment\` does **not** define that attribute. Every call raises \`AttributeError\`, gets swallowed by a broad \`except Exception\` handler, and returns \`False\`. The misleading log line \`Failed to parse service URL for validation: <url>\` is the giveaway — \`urlparse()\` doesn't throw on real URLs, the \`AttributeError\` does. The whole \`additional_allowed_domains\` mechanism is dead code as a result, so the plugin's JWT validation rejects every \`serviceUrl\` that isn't on the SDK's hardcoded Teams allowlist.

This is the entire reason **Web Chat / Bot Framework Emulator / Direct Line** all silently 401 on inbound activities at JWT validation time when running the plugin against \`2.0.0a78\`.

In \`2.0.0\` stable, \`is_allowed_service_url()\` and \`additional_allowed_domains\` are **removed entirely** in favor of strict per-request equality between the JWT \`serviceurl\` claim and the activity's actual \`serviceUrl\` (which is a much better security model). Migrating to \`2.0.0\` stable makes this whole class of failure go away.

### 2. The current alpha pin is fragile

\`pip install microsoft-teams-apps\` (no version) currently resolves to \`2.0.0\` stable, which restructured \`App()\` to accept a single \`AppOptions\` instance. Any unpinned downstream install crash-loops with:

\`\`\`
InternalAppOptions.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'client_id'
\`\`\`

Pinning to \`2.0.0a78\` works around it but means downstream operators have to know to pin, and we're stuck on alpha until the migration lands.

### 3. The alpha series is unmaintained

Looking at the \`microsoft-teams-apps\` PyPI release history, \`2.0.0a78\` is the last alpha (2026-04-25), and \`2.0.0\` shipped 5 days later. The alpha series is unlikely to receive any further fixes.

## Proposed scope

- Migrate \`plugins/platforms/teams/adapter.py\` \`App()\` construction to \`AppOptions\` (or whichever pattern the maintainers prefer).
- Sweep the imports/usage for any other 2.0.0 stable API drift (auth validators, activity senders, etc.).
- Update \`pyproject.toml\` / install docs to require \`microsoft-teams-apps>=2.0.0\` instead of the alpha pin.
- Verify Web Chat / Emulator round-trip works under \`2.0.0\` stable (the new strict-equality validator should naturally accept inbound activities since the plugin gets the \`serviceUrl\` from the activity itself).

## Help offered

I'm happy to take a swing at the migration if useful — the plugin is the only file in the repo that needs touching for the SDK API change, and the test surface is the same Web Chat / Emulator / Teams round-trip we already have. Happy to coordinate with @aamirj-msft or whoever owns the plugin since they've also been driving the upstream SDK release. Let me know if a draft PR would be welcome or if you'd rather have it done in-house.

## Related

- PR #18331 — \`fix(teams): route plain-text replies and typing via per-conversation serviceUrl\` (independent of this migration; the per-conversation routing concern survives the SDK API change).

items.body:
## Bug Description

In `agent/auxiliary_client.py`, `resolve_provider_client()` receives an `explicit_api_key` parameter and correctly propagates it to most downstream provider calls. However, when routing to OpenRouter, it calls `_try_openrouter()` **without** passing `explicit_api_key`, silently ignoring it.

This causes auth failures when the auxiliary client falls back to OpenRouter using a runtime API key from the credential pool.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a credential pool entry for `openrouter` with a valid runtime API key
2. Set a main provider (e.g., `openai` or `openrouter`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY`
3. When the main call fails and the system falls back to `openrouter` via `resolve_provider_client()`
4. OpenRouter fallback uses env var `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (may be empty) instead of the pool's runtime key

## Expected Behavior

OpenRouter fallback should use the `explicit_api_key` passed to `resolve_provider_client`, just like all other providers do.

## Root Cause Analysis

**File:** `agent/auxiliary_client.py`, line ~2052

```python
def resolve_provider_client(
    provider: str,
    ...
    explicit_api_key: str = None,  # received here
    ...
):
    ...
    if provider == "openrouter":
        client, default = _try_openrouter()  # explicit_api_key dropped!
```

The `_try_openrouter()` function has no parameter to accept `explicit_api_key`, so even callers that want to pass it cannot.

## Proposed Fix

1. Add `explicit_api_key: str = None` parameter to `_try_openrouter()`
2. Use `explicit_api_key or os.getenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY")` as the key source
3. Update call site: `_try_openrouter(explicit_api_key=explicit_api_key)`

## Affected Component

- [x] Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

## Environment

- Hermes v0.12.0 (v2026.4.30)

## Problem

Currently, pinning a skill locks it from both curator deletion *and* agent edits (skill_manage patch/edit actions). These are two different concerns that should not be conflated.

## Expected behavior

- Pinned skills: agents **can** still patch/edit them to improve content

- Pinned skills: curator cannot remove them ✅
- Pinned skills: agents cannot edit them ❌ — forces an unpin → edit → re-pin workflow that discourages skill maintenance

Skills get pinned to survive curator passes, but they still need to evolve as workflows are refined. The current behavior creates friction that makes skills go stale over time — agents (and users) are less likely to improve a skill if it requires an unpin/re-pin dance every time.

items.title: Curator should not auto-archive user-created custom skills without dry-run/approval

labels.name: comp/agent

labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

After updating to the Curator release (`v2026.4.30`), Curator auto-ran on my live Hermes install and consolidated/archived a large number of personally-created custom workflow skills without a dry-run report or approval step.

I checked the local logs after filing this. I did **not** manually run `hermes curator run`. The run was launched by the gateway cron ticker calling Curator in the background.

This is related to the Curator work introduced around PR #16049 / the Curator RFC #16077.

## What happened

Curator ran as an automatic background maintenance pass on a live install. The run archived skills by consolidation, not by stale pruning:

- agent-created skills before: 87
- after: 45
- archived/consolidated in the run: 54
- stale/unused prunings without merge target: 0
- new umbrella skills created: 12

The archived items included many personal/custom workflow skills that I had intentionally created for private workflows and project-specific operating procedures. I am intentionally not listing those skill names publicly here, but they were not disposable one-off skills from Hermes' own self-improvement loop.

## Evidence that this was an automatic run

Local logs show:

- The gateway log recorded a Curator completion message from a background Curator session.
- The Curator session transcript begins with the internal prompt: `You are running as Hermes' background skill CURATOR...`
- There was no shell history entry for `hermes curator run`.
- The gateway source currently calls Curator from the cron ticker path:
  - `gateway/run.py` calls `maybe_run_curator(idle_for_seconds=float("inf"), ...)`
- Curator defaults to enabled when no config disables it:
  - `agent/curator.py` returns `cfg.get("enabled", True)`
- With no prior `last_run_at`, `should_run_now()` returns true.

So the precise issue is not "the update command directly ran Curator." The issue is that after the update, the gateway's background ticker auto-launched Curator because it was enabled by default and had no prior run state.

## Problem

As a user, I had no clear way to distinguish:

- skills created by Hermes itself during self-improvement
- skills I personally created for custom workflows
- skills installed from a hub/bundled source
- skills that should never be touched without explicit approval

Curator appears to treat "not bundled / not hub-installed" as eligible for curation. That means user-authored custom skills and Hermes-authored temporary skills can collapse into the same bucket, which is dangerous.

The first run should not mutate a live skill library automatically. It should generate a review report first.

## Expected behavior

For a live user install, Curator should be opt-in or report-first by default. A safer flow would be:

1. Curator takes an explicit target path / Hermes home / skills path.
2. It runs in dry-run mode first.
3. It writes a report showing exactly what it would archive, consolidate, or patch.
4. It explains why for each proposed action.
5. It requires explicit user confirmation before modifying anything.
6. It provides a clear way to mark/pin user-authored custom skills before the first live run.

## Actual behavior

Curator auto-ran from the gateway background ticker and performed live consolidation/archival. It did preserve archived copies, but that is still a disruptive mutation because many custom skills are individually invokable workflows. Flattening them into broad umbrella skills changes discovery, invocation, profile behavior, and operational assumptions.

## Why this matters

items.title: [Feature]:  Anchor-based editing mode for patch tool

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

 The patch tool's replace mode relies on fuzzy matching to find old_string.
  The 9-strategy chain handles many edge cases, but fails on a common real-world
  pattern: files with repeated or near-identical lines.

  Example — a Python service with validation in both login() and register():

      def login(self, username, password):
          if not username:
              return {"error": "username required"}    # line 4
          ...

      def register(self, username, password):
          if not username:
              return {"error": "username required"}    # line 14
          ...

  Editing the return in register() fails with "Found 2 matches". The model must
  add enough surrounding context to disambiguate — which it often gets wrong on
  the first try, wasting iterations. This is the single biggest source of failed
  edits I encounter in practice.

### Proposed Solution

 Add a hashline mode to the patch tool that uses content-hash line anchors:

  1. read_file(hashline=True) outputs each line with a 4-char content hash:

         4:k9dt|            return {"error": "username required"}
         ...
         14:k9dt#2|            return {"error": "username required"}

  2. patch(mode="hashline", anchor_range="k9dt#2:k9dt#2", new_content=...)
     edits by anchor. Collision-disambiguated with #1/#2 suffixes.

  The model copies the 4-char hash from the read output — no need to reproduce
  surrounding code. O(1) lookup, zero ambiguity.

  Design:
  - Hash: 4-char base36 (SHA-256 truncated). 1.68M values, collision bound ~1296 lines.
  - Staleness guard: anchors validated before writing; stale anchors return
    "Did you mean?" suggestions.
  - Opt-in: all new params default off (hashline=False, mode="replace").
    Zero impact on existing behavior.
  - stdlib only (hashlib, re, difflib). No new dependencies.
  - Inspiration: oh-my-pi (github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi) which uses BPE bigram
    hashes for specific tokenizers. This uses generic base36 for cross-model
    compatibility.

### Alternatives Considered

 1. Improve fuzzy match — more heuristics help at the margins but can't solve
     the fundamental ambiguity of repeated content.
  2. Make the model add more context — prompt engineering helps but burns tokens
     and still fails on large files with deeply nested duplicates.
  3. Use V4A patch format — works for multi-file edits but overkill for single-
     line changes and still requires context lines.

  Hashline complements these approaches. It's most valuable when the other modes
  fail, and falls back naturally — the model can still use replace mode for
  simple edits.

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

I’m running Hermes dashboard behind a Traefik reverse proxy and the dashboard UI works great, but Chat fails because the dashboard websocket endpoints are rejected with `4403 client_host_not_loopback`.

## Environment
    
- Hermes Agent version: v0.12.0 (2026.4.30)
- Dashboard launched via a systemd user service
- Reverse proxy: Traefik
- Hermes agent, hermes dashboard and Traefik proxy are on the same host server
- Browser connects to:
  - `https://hermes.local.anondomain.com`
- Traefik proxies to:
   - `http://127.0.0.1:9119`
- Dashboard access, via proxy, limited to authenticated users by Authentik. 

## Symptoms
    
Browser console shows websocket failures for:

- `/api/ws`
- `/api/events`
- `/api/pty`

## Example frontend error:

- `events feed disconnected — tool calls may not appear`

## What I've tested 
 
- Dashboard dependencies are installed and working
- Normal dashboard pages load correctly

- Tried different dashboard arguments including:
  - `--host 127.0.0.1 --port 9119 --no-open`
  - `--host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119 --no-open --insecure`

- Set Traefik passHostHeader: false
- Verified upstream requests from the Traefik proxy use:
  - Host: `127.0.0.1:9119`
  
## TCPDUMP packet capture / proxy evidence

Traefik forwards websocket upgrade requests like:

```text
http
GET /api/ws?... HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:9119
Connection: Upgrade
Upgrade: websocket
X-Forwarded-For: 192.168.xx.xx # anonymised laptop IP
X-Forwarded-Port: 443
X-Forwarded-Proto: https
X-Real-Ip: 127.0.0.1
```
Hermes responds with `403 Forbidden`.

## Added temporary logging to Hermes web server

I temporarily added logging to `hermes_cli/web_server.py` and captured:
    
```text
Dashboard websocket close: endpoint=/api/ws code=4403 reason=client_host_not_loopback ctx={
  'path': '/api/ws',
  'client_host': '192.168.10.70',
  'client_port': 0,
  'host': '127.0.0.1:9119',
  'origin': 'https://hermes.local.anondomain.com', # anonymised
  'x_forwarded_for': '192.168.xx.xx', # anonymised laptop IP
  'x_real_ip': '127.0.0.1',
  'x_forwarded_host': '',
  'x_forwarded_proto': 'https',
  'x_forwarded_port': '443',
  'upgrade': 'websocket',
  'connection': 'Upgrade',
  'has_token': True,
  'token_prefix': '3M2pQKH_',
  'channel': ''
}
```

Similar entries occur for:

- `/api/events`
- `/api/pty`
    
## Root cause
    
The dashboard websocket handlers reject when:

```python
client_host = ws.client.host if ws.client else ""
if client_host and client_host not in _LOOPBACK_HOSTS:
    await ws.close(code=4403)
```

In a reverse proxy deployment, `ws.client.host` becomes the original browser IP rather than loopback, so chat is unusable even when the reverse proxy is on the same host and the upstream target is `127.0.0.1`.
    

### Proposed Solution

Please make Hermes dashboard chat usable behind a trusted reverse proxy, for example by one of:

1. making the loopback-only websocket restriction configurable
2. disabling proxy-derived client-IP enforcement for dashboard websocket endpoints
3. using a different trust model when the dashboard is intentionally run with `--insecure`
4. allowing trusted same-host reverse proxy deployments explicitly

### Alternatives Considered

I've tried many different configurations to 'trick' the Hermes web server to no avail. 
I don't want to add a messaging gateway to all Hermes profiles (those with sandboxed BE's already have messaging) or to install a desktop and browser on the server to access dashboard chat. There may be different proxies that can handle it differently but I believe this is a sensible change that other users may need.

### Problem or Use Case

I'm using Hermes as a multi-agent operating system for a product-intelligence pipeline. The key requirement is not just “spawn subagents,” but **orchestrate named persistent specialist profiles that have their own runtime, model, tools, memory/docs, and output contracts**.

setup is essentially a pipeline and looks roughly like this:

- **Orchestrator** = executive/orchestrator profile. Plans work, writes task files, validates outputs, updates docs, makes go/no-go decisions.
- **Scraper** = scraping agent. Gather relevant data and is the pipeline intake.
- **Refiner** = data refinement agent/runtime. Converts raw harvested evidence into structured data (runs locally on my RTX 5090 via llama server)
- **Analyser** = sentiment analysis and interpretation.
- **Synthesizer** = writes the final output.

Each agent runs on a different model according to required capabilities and cost profile.

The workflow is pipeline-shaped:

`Harvest → Refine → Validate → Translate → Synthesize`

Each stage needs to run as the **actual named profile**, not just a generic delegated subagent inheriting the orchestrator's model. That distinction matters a lot for me. If I say “delegate to Scribe” or “run Forge (refiner)” I need Hermes to use that profile’s real configured model, system prompt, tools, `.env`, working directory, and memory. Same-model delegation is useful for quick subtasks, but it is not true profile orchestration.



### Proposed Solution

What would improve the  workflow most:

1. **First-class profile invocation from inside Hermes**
   - Something like `run_profile(profile="forge", task=..., workdir=..., output_contract=...)`
   - It should use the real profile config, not inherit the parent model.

2. **Structured handoff between profiles**
   - Ability to pass files/artifacts explicitly from one profile to the next.
   - Ideally each profile run declares expected input paths, output paths, and schemas.

3. **Profile run observability** 
Orchestrator needs to see status, logs, final output file paths, errors, token/model info, and whether the profile actually wrote the expected artifact.
“ok” is not enough; need verifiable completion.

4. **Pipeline orchestration primitives**
   - Define a DAG or sequential pipeline:
     - run Scraper
     - validate scraper output
     - run refiner
     - validate claim schema
     - run sentiment analyser
     - stop if quality gate fails
   - Support retries, pause/resume, and per-stage failure handling.

5. **Per-profile runtime integrity**
   - I need confirmation of which model/provider/profile actually ran.
   - Especially important because some agents use local llama on an RTX 5090, while orchestrator may use a frontier hosted model.
   - If Hermes silently runs the wrong model, the whole workflow becomes untrustworthy.

6. **Artifact-centered session memory**
   - Long workflows should persist around files and run manifests, not just chat history.
   - Need resumable runs: “continue pipeline V7 from sentiment analyser failure” should reload the right artifacts and state.

The big idea: I don’t want a swarm of anonymous chatbots. I need **named production roles with contracts**, where the orchestrator can orchestrate them like services: call them, pass artifacts, verify outputs, and stop the line when a quality gate fails. 

The whole pipeline should be automation capable, where the probabilistic aspects are minimized and outcomes become standardized/deterministic

Tl;dr The ask is named persistent specialist profiles with their own runtime integrity, explicit artifact handoff, validation, observability, pause/resume, and pipeline failure handling

### Alternatives Considered

Currently I handle this manually. I have my orchestrator directly steer the other agents invoking their own profiles and then create handoff documents for the next stage in the pipeline, copying context back and forth as needed. This causes each stage of the pipeline to have its own orchestrator instance, who manages the specialist agent in that part of the pipeline. I essentially copy context/status messages between multiple instances of the same orchestrator between sessions/pipeline stages to coordinate the entire pipeline

items.body:
# fix: voice_mode OSError from missing PortAudio misreported as missing Python packages

## Bug Description

When PortAudio system library (`libportaudio2`) is not installed, `/voice on` reports:

```
Audio capture: MISSING (pip install sounddevice numpy)
```

This is misleading for two reasons:

1. **Wrong diagnosis**: `sounddevice` and `numpy` may already be installed. The real issue is that `import sounddevice` raises **OSError** (not `ImportError`) when the PortAudio shared library is missing, and `_audio_available()` treats both exceptions identically, resulting in an incorrect "packages missing" message.
2. **Invalid fix command**: Hermes creates its venv via `uv venv` without `--seed`, so **pip is not present** in the venv by default. The suggested `python -m pip install sounddevice numpy` fails with `No module named pip`. Even if pip is manually installed, uv won't track those packages — they may be lost on the next `uv sync`.

## Root Cause

### 1. OSError misidentified as missing packages

In `tools/voice_mode.py`, `_audio_available()` catches both `(ImportError, OSError)` and returns `False`:

```python
def _audio_available() -> bool:
    try:
        _import_audio()
        return True
    except (ImportError, OSError):  # ← OSError ≠ missing packages
        return False
```

When PortAudio is absent, `import sounddevice` raises `OSError`, which is treated as "packages not installed".

### 2. venv lacks pip by default

`scripts/install.sh` creates the venv with `uv venv venv --python "$PYTHON_VERSION"` (line ~908) without passing `--seed`, so pip is not included. This is standard for uv-managed projects, but the error message assumes pip exists.

## Suggested Fix

### Fix 1: Distinguish the two failure modes

```python
def _audio_available() -> bool:
    try:
        import sounddevice as sd
        import numpy as np
        return True
    except ImportError:
        return False  # Python packages missing
    except OSError:
        return False  # PortAudio system library missing — report differently
```

And update `voice_status()` / `_voice_capture_install_hint()` to provide context-appropriate guidance:
- **ImportError** → `"uv sync --extra voice"` (for uv-managed installs)
- **OSError** → `"sudo apt-get install libportaudio2"` / `"brew install portaudio"` (PortAudio system library missing)

### Fix 2: Use uv commands instead of pip

The install hint should use `uv sync --extra voice` instead of `python -m pip install sounddevice numpy`, matching the project's package management approach.

## Environment

- Hermes version: 0.12.0
- OS: WSL2 (Ubuntu, Python 3.11)
- `sounddevice==0.5.5`, `numpy==2.4.4` — both installed in venv
- `libportaudio2` was **not** installed at the time of the error

## Related Source

- `tools/voice_mode.py`: `_audio_available()` (line 43), `voice_status()` (~line 930)
- `scripts/install.sh`: `setup_venv()` (line ~908) — `uv venv` without `--seed`

items.title: feat(discord): auto-rename threads from generated session titles
items.body:
## Feature Description

Add an option for the Discord gateway to automatically rename Discord threads/sub-sessions using Hermes' generated session title.

Hermes already has two related pieces:

- `agent/title_generator.py` auto-generates short session titles after the first user/assistant exchange and stores them in the session DB.
- `gateway/platforms/discord.py` supports `discord.auto_thread` and auto-creates a Discord thread on @mention. The current thread name is derived from the initial user message, stripped of mentions and truncated.

Currently these are not connected: the generated Hermes session title updates the internal session DB only, but the Discord thread name remains the raw first-message-derived title.

## Motivation

Discord auto-threading is useful for isolating conversations, but the initial message is often not a good thread title:

- It may contain a long prompt, partial context, or an @mention-stripped fragment.
- The real topic often becomes clear only after the first response.
- Hermes already computes a better 3–7 word session title, but users only see it in Hermes session metadata, not in the Discord UI.

Syncing the generated session title to the Discord thread name would make Discord conversation lists much easier to scan and resume.

## Proposed Solution

Add a Discord config option, for example:

```yaml
discord:
  auto_thread: true
  auto_rename_threads: true
```

When enabled:

1. After `maybe_auto_title(...)` generates and stores a title for a Discord session, detect whether the session source is a Discord thread.
2. If the thread was auto-created by Hermes, call Discord's thread edit API, e.g. `thread.edit(name=generated_title)`.
3. Sanitize/truncate the title according to Discord thread name limits.
4. Fail gracefully/log a warning if the bot lacks permission to manage/edit the thread.

Suggested implementation areas:

- `agent/title_generator.py` could expose/accept a completion callback after `set_session_title(...)` succeeds, or return the generated title through a gateway wrapper.
- `gateway/run.py` currently calls `maybe_auto_title(...)` for gateway sessions after the response completes.
- `gateway/platforms/discord.py` already has access to Discord client/thread objects and auto-thread metadata.

## Behavior Details / Guardrails

- Default could be `false` if maintainers want conservative behavior, or `true` only for Hermes-created auto threads.
- Should not rename arbitrary user-created threads unless explicitly configured.
- Should not overwrite a manually set Discord thread name after a user changes it, if detectable.
- Should not rename when `/title` is used unless a separate option supports manual sync.
- Should preserve the existing `/title` behavior for Hermes internal session naming.

## Alternatives Considered

- Keep the current first-message-derived thread name. This works but produces noisy or low-quality thread names.
- Require users to manually rename threads. This defeats the point of auto-threaded sessions.
- Make `/title` update Discord thread names. Useful, but it does not solve the automatic naming case after first exchange.

## Related Code Observed

- `agent/title_generator.py`: `maybe_auto_title(...)`, `auto_title_session(...)`
- `gateway/run.py`: gateway calls `maybe_auto_title(...)` after final response
- `gateway/platforms/discord.py`: `_auto_create_thread(...)`, `discord.auto_thread`, `DISCORD_AUTO_THREAD`, `DISCORD_NO_THREAD_CHANNELS`

- `model_tools.py` - `_run_async()`

May 1 08:17 - OOM kill, memory peak: 8.0 GB + 0B swap (MemoryMax=8G, MemorySwapMax=0)

items.body:
## Bug Report

### Summary
Clicking the resume button (triangle) on the Sessions page in the dashboard does not restore the selected session. The chat tab opens but shows a fresh empty session instead of the resumed conversation.

### Environment
- **Hermes Agent version:** v0.12.0 (2026.4.30)
- **Platform:** macOS (Mac Mini M4, Darwin 25.4.0 arm64)
- **Dashboard:** started with `hermes dashboard --tui --insecure --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119`
- **Browser:** Chromium-based (also confirmed via WebSocket test that `session.resume` RPC works correctly)

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Start Hermes dashboard with `--tui` flag
2. Have at least one session with messages in the database
3. Navigate to the **Sessions** page in the dashboard
4. Click the **resume button (triangle icon)** on a session row
5. The URL changes to `/chat?resume=<session_id>` and the Chat tab becomes visible
6. **Bug:** The chat tab shows a fresh empty session, NOT the resumed conversation

### Expected Behavior
The chat tab should load the selected session history and continue that conversation.

### Actual Behavior
A new empty session is created. The `resume` query parameter is ignored.

### Root Cause
In `web/src/pages/ChatPage.tsx`, line 150:

```typescript
const resumeRef = useRef<string | null>(searchParams.get("resume"));
```

`useRef` only sets its value **once** at mount time. The `ChatPage` component is rendered as a **persistent component** (always mounted, hidden via `display:none` when not on `/chat` — see `App.tsx` line 613). This is by design so the PTY WebSocket survives tab switches (commit d293e0051).

The main `useEffect` that creates the WebSocket depends on `[channel]`, where `channel` is generated once via `useMemo(() => generateChannelId(), [])`. So the effect **never re-runs** after mount.

When the user navigates from `/sessions` to `/chat?resume=SESSION_ID`:
1. `searchParams` updates (new `resume` param)
2. But `resumeRef.current` stays `null` (from initial mount without resume)
3. The existing WebSocket (without `resume` param) remains connected
4. `buildWsUrl()` uses `resumeRef.current` which is still `null`
5. The PTY child starts a fresh session instead of resuming

### Workaround / Fix
I applied the following patch locally which resolves the issue:

```typescript
const resumeRef = useRef<string | null>(searchParams.get("resume"));
const channel = useMemo(() => generateChannelId(), []);

// Keep resumeRef in sync with searchParams so that navigating from
// /sessions to /chat?resume=SESSION_ID picks up the new resume target.
// Without this, the persistent ChatPage component keeps the initial
// resume value (null) and the PTY WebSocket never gets the resume param.
const [resumeKey, setResumeKey] = useState(0);
useEffect(() => {
  const next = searchParams.get("resume");
  if (next !== resumeRef.current) {
    resumeRef.current = next;
    setResumeKey((k) => k + 1); // bump to force WS reconnect
  }
}, [searchParams]);
```

And changed the main useEffect dependency from:
```typescript
}, [channel]);
```
to:
```typescript
}, [channel, resumeKey]);
```

This forces a WebSocket reconnection with the correct `resume` parameter when the user navigates to `/chat?resume=<id>`.

### Additional Context
- The `session.resume` JSON-RPC method itself works correctly (tested via direct WebSocket connection)
- The `database is locked` SQLite warning in gateway logs is a separate issue (busy_timeout=0) but not the primary cause
- This bug affects all users who use the dashboard with `--tui` and try to resume sessions via the Sessions page

### Verified
- Confirmed that the WebSocket receives the `resume` param correctly after the fix
- Confirmed the PTY child shows "resuming…" in the terminal output
- Dashboard rebuilt and tested on the affected system

### Bug Description


# Kanban DB is profile-scoped instead of shared across profiles, so workers cannot see root tasks

## Summary

The Kanban documentation says the board is shared across all Hermes profiles and that tasks live in `~/.hermes/kanban.db`.

However, when using multiple profiles, Kanban appears to resolve `kanban.db` relative to the active profile `HERMES_HOME`. This creates separate boards per profile, for example:

- default/root profile: `~/.hermes/kanban.db`
- `frontend-coder` profile: `~/.hermes/profiles/frontend-coder/kanban.db`

As a result, tasks created from the default profile are visible with:

```bash
hermes profile use default
hermes kanban list
````

but not visible from another profile:

```bash
hermes profile use frontend-coder
hermes kanban list
```

This also breaks Kanban workers: the dispatcher can spawn a worker for a task, but the worker profile looks in its own profile-local DB and reports that the task does not exist.

## Example error from worker

```text
Query: work kanban task t_c2cea64d
Initializing agent...
────────────────────────────────────────

  ┊ ⚡ kanban_sh   0.0s [error]
  ┊ ⚡ kanban_sh   0.0s [error]
 ─  ⚕ Hermes  ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 

     The task t_c2cea64d doesn't exist in the kanban board. It may have
     been archived, deleted, or the ID could be incorrect.

     Can you double-check the task ID? Or if you meant a different task,
     point me to it and I'll pick it up.
```

## Environment / setup

* OS: WSL Ubuntu
* Hermes installed under: `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`
* Profiles used:

  * `default`
  * `frontend-coder`
* Observed DB files:

  * `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\user\.hermes\kanban.db`
  * `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\user\.hermes\profiles\frontend-coder\kanban.db`

Relevant commit I was looking at:

[https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/c868425467502f4ffa9757e731477cf91262fa3f](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/c868425467502f4ffa9757e731477cf91262fa3f)

## Suspected cause

The Kanban DB path appears to be resolved from the active `HERMES_HOME`.

Current behavior seems equivalent to:

```python
get_hermes_home() / "kanban.db"
```

Since profiles set `HERMES_HOME` to:

```text
~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>
```

this makes Kanban profile-scoped instead of shared.

## Proposed fix

Use the default Hermes root for Kanban storage instead of the active profile home.

For example, in `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`:

```python
def kanban_db_path() -> Path:
    """Return the path to the shared host-level kanban.db, independent of active profile."""
    from hermes_constants import get_default_hermes_root
    return get_default_hermes_root() / "kanban.db"


def workspaces_root() -> Path:
    """Return the shared directory under which scratch workspaces are created."""
    from hermes_constants import get_default_hermes_root
    return get_default_hermes_root() / "kanban" / "workspaces"
```

There may also be other Kanban-related paths that should be shared rather than profile-local, for example:

* worker logs
* Kanban workspaces
* dispatcher/gateway Kanban paths
* any code path used by worker tools like `kanban_show`, `kanban_complete`, etc.

## Why this matters

The docs describe Kanban as the primitive for multi-agent, multi-profile collaboration:

> shared across all your Hermes profiles

But with the current behavior, each profile can silently get its own isolated board. This makes cross-profile task assignment unreliable and causes spawned workers to fail even when the task exists in the root board.

## Extra note

After patching `kanban_db_path()` and `workspaces_root()` locally to use `get_default_hermes_root()`, I then hit a separate gateway service issue when running from the `frontend-coder` profile:

```text
Failed to start hermes-gateway-frontend-coder.service: Unit hermes-gateway-frontend-coder.service not found.
```

That seems separate from the Kanban DB issue, but it may be related to profile-specific gateway/service behavior. My main concern in this issue is that Kanban storage appears profile-scoped despite the docs saying it should be shared.

```


### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
# 1. Use default/root profile
hermes profile use default

# 2. Initialize/create a Kanban task
hermes kanban init
hermes kanban create "test task for frontend coder" --assignee frontend-coder

# 3. Confirm task exists in default profile
hermes kanban list

# 4. Switch to another profile
hermes profile use frontend-coder

# 5. Try to list/show the same task
hermes kanban list
hermes kanban show <task_id>
```

### Expected Behavior

Kanban should be host-level and profile-agnostic, as described in the docs.

All profiles on the same host should read/write the same board:

```text
~/.hermes/kanban.db
```

So the following should show the same tasks:

```bash
hermes profile use default
hermes kanban list

hermes profile use frontend-coder
hermes kanban list
```

And a worker spawned as `frontend-coder` should be able to call Kanban tools against a task created from the default/root profile.



### Actual Behavior

The `frontend-coder` profile does not see the task.

A separate DB exists at:

```text
~/.hermes/profiles/frontend-coder/kanban.db
```

The worker also fails with “task does not exist” because it appears to look up the task in the profile-local DB instead of the shared root DB.

items.title: [Feature]: Support multiple independent questions in clarify tool
items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

The `clarify` tool currently accepts only one `question` parameter (a single string). When the agent needs to ask the user multiple independent questions, the only workaround is to concatenate them into one composite question and offer composite choices (e.g. combining "How do you feel?" + "What color do you like?" into one question with choices like "Feeling good, likes blue" / "Feeling tired, likes red" — each choice encoding answers to both questions). This does not scale: 2 questions x 4 choices each = 16 composite options; 3 questions x 3 choices each = 27. The UX degrades rapidly and the agent effectively cannot batch more than 2 small clarification needs at once.

Real-world example from use: agent wants to ask (1) user preference on approach A vs B, and (2) user availability timeline. These are independent dimensions — forcing them into a single composite question is unnatural and the combinatorial explosion of choices makes it impractical.

## Proposed Solution

Add an optional `questions` array parameter alongside the existing single-`question` parameter. Each question object has its own `question` text and optional `choices` array. The rendering layer (CLI prompt_toolkit, TUI, gateway adapters) presents them as separate widgets/forms, and the tool returns an array of answers keyed by question index or id.

Example schema addition:

```json
{
  "questions": {
    "type": "array",
    "description": "Multiple independent questions to ask at once. Use instead of single-question when you have 2+ independent clarification needs.",
    "maxItems": 5,
    "items": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "id": {
          "type": "string",
          "description": "Short identifier for matching responses (e.g. 'approach', 'timeline')"
        },
        "question": {
          "type": "string",
          "description": "The question text"
        },
        "choices": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {"type": "string"},
          "maxItems": 4,
          "description": "Up to 4 answer choices. Omit for open-ended text input."
        }
      },
      "required": ["question"]
    }
  }
}
```

Backward compatibility: the existing single-`question` parameter remains untouched. When `questions` is present, it takes precedence and the single-question parameter is ignored.

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Composite question + composite choices (current workaround)**: Works for 2 small questions but does not scale. 3+ questions become combinatorially impossible.
2. **Multiple sequential `clarify` calls**: Works but wastes conversation turns and context tokens. The agent cannot efficiently batch multiple independent clarification needs.
3. **Free-text multi-question with no structured choices**: Loses the structured choice UX that makes `clarify` useful. Harder for the agent to parse free-form multi-answer responses reliably.
4. **Agent-side heuristics to skip unnecessary questions**: Not always applicable — sometimes multiple independent decisions genuinely need user input.

items.title: [Bug]: CLOSE_WAIT fd leak causes all platforms to stop responding after ~1-2 hours

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Description

All messaging platforms (QQ Bot, Feishu/Lark) stop responding simultaneously after ~1-2 hours of uptime. The root cause is a **file descriptor leak** -- TCP sockets accumulate in `CLOSE_WAIT` state until the process hits macOS default soft limit of 256.

## Symptoms

- QQ Bot and Feishu both go silent at the same time
- Logs show: `[Errno 24] Too many open files`
- Feishu SDK retries fail: `connect failed, err: [Errno 24] Too many open files`
- `lsof -p <PID> | grep CLOSE_WAIT` shows 200+ leaked connections
- `kanban notifier tick failed: unable to open database file` (secondary effect)

## Root Cause

The Feishu SDK (lark-oapi) and/or the HTTP client used for API calls leak TCP connections. Each API call (LLM requests, tool calls, message sending) leaves a socket in `CLOSE_WAIT` state. After ~200 leaked connections, the process exhausts its file descriptor limit (macOS soft limit: 256), causing **all** new network requests to fail -- not just Feishu, but also QQ Bot, LLM API calls, MCP servers, etc.

## Environment

- **Hermes version**: v0.12.0 (2026.4.30)
- **Python**: 3.14.4
- **OS**: macOS (Apple Silicon)
- **Platforms**: QQ Bot + Feishu (both affected)
- **Warp**: Enabled (all CLOSE_WAIT connections route through `connectivity-check.warp-svc`)

## Reproduction Steps

1. Start gateway with QQ Bot + Feishu platforms
2. Wait 1-2 hours with moderate message traffic
3. `lsof -p <PID> | grep CLOSE_WAIT | wc -l` grows steadily
4. When CLOSE_WAIT > 200, all platforms stop responding
5. `hermes gateway restart` fixes it temporarily

## Evidence

```
$ lsof -p <PID> -i TCP | grep CLOSE_WAIT | wc -l
215

$ lsof -p <PID> | wc -l
353

$ ulimit -n
256

# All CLOSE_WAIT connections route through Warp proxy:
$ lsof -p <PID> -i TCP | grep CLOSE_WAIT | awk '{print $9}' | head -5
connectivity-check.warp-svc:57890->43.159.235.46:https
connectivity-check.warp-svc:57885->43.159.235.46:https
```

## Workaround (currently in place)

- Cron job monitoring CLOSE_WAIT count every 10 minutes
- Auto-restart when CLOSE_WAIT > 30 or FD count > 200
- Increased macOS fd limit via launchd SoftResourceLimits

## Suggested Fix

The underlying issue is in the HTTP connection pool management. Connections should be properly closed/released after each API call, not left in `CLOSE_WAIT` state. This likely requires:

1. Ensuring aiohttp sessions are properly closed after each request
2. Or adding connection pool cleanup/reaping logic
3. Investigating whether Warp proxy exacerbates the issue (all leaked connections go through Warp)

## Related

This is the same root cause as the QQ Bot 4009 "Session timed out" disconnects -- fd exhaustion prevents the adapter from maintaining WebSocket heartbeats.

**Summary:** Please consider making Hermes sessions portable across interfaces so a user can start in terminal, continue the same session from Telegram/Discord/Slack/Teams, and later return to terminal. `/title`, `/new`, and `/resume` are a strong start, but session identity, endpoint bindings, and remote resume visibility need to become first-class. Related idea: a higher-level **project** concept could retain supporting docs and related sessions in shared context.

---

Hermes should treat the **session** as the primary object, not the transport.

Today, Hermes already has useful session controls like:

- `/title`
- `/new`
- `/resume`

Those work well as Hermes-side session management, but the experience across gateway platforms still feels incomplete. In practice, users cannot reliably:

- start a session in terminal
- continue that same session from Telegram / Discord / Slack / Teams
- return later to terminal
- clearly see what remote endpoint is bound to what session

At the same time, UI surfaces such as **hermes-webui**, **AionUI**, and **hermes-desktop** are already moving toward richer session/workspace continuity. Gateway platforms should keep pace.

## Why this matters

A strong Hermes workflow should be:

> start in terminal → continue remotely from phone/chat → return to desktop later

That is much more powerful than merely having multiple disconnected entry points into Hermes.

This would improve:

- mobile continuation
- async workflows
- long-running task follow-up
- product coherence across surfaces
- the feeling of “one agent, many interfaces”

---

## Current gaps

### 1. Session identity is weaker than transport identity
A Hermes session exists, but it is not always visible or addressable as a first-class remote target.

### 2. Session labels are not the same as remote routing
`/title` is useful, but it is often just a Hermes-side label, not a guaranteed mapping to a Telegram topic / Discord thread / Slack thread.

### 3. Cross-surface continuation is not first-class
Users cannot naturally resume a terminal-origin session from a messaging platform.

### 4. Verification and visibility are weak
It is not always clear:

- what session is active
- what endpoint it is bound to
- whether it is remotely resumable
- whether a platform thread is actually linked to a Hermes session

---

## Proposal

Introduce a first-class model for:

1. **session identity**
2. **endpoint bindings**
3. **cross-surface attachment/resume**

### Core idea
A Hermes session should be able to exist independently of:

- CLI
- Telegram
- Discord
- Slack
- Teams
- web UI
- desktop UI

A user should be able to attach to the same session from multiple supported surfaces over time.

---

## Suggested MVP

### A. Make session bindings visible
Add a way to inspect:

- session title
- session id
- origin surface
- current endpoint binding(s)
- remote attach/resume eligibility

Possible commands/tooling:

- `/sessions`
- `/where`
- session route inspection tooling

### B. Allow cross-surface resume/attach
Support workflows like:

- start in CLI
- `/title eco-refactor`
- later in Telegram: `/resume eco-refactor`

and the reverse:

- start in Telegram
- later in CLI: `hermes --resume eco-refactor`

### C. Clarify label vs thread semantics
Hermes should clearly distinguish:

- **Hermes session title**
- **platform endpoint**
- **platform thread/topic**
- **binding between them**

This avoids confusion where `/title` appears to imply native platform routing when it may not.

---

## Design direction

### Session as top-level object
A session should have metadata like:

- `session_id`
- `title`
- `origin_surface`
- `created_at`
- `updated_at`
- `remote_attach_enabled`
- `linked_endpoints[]`

### Endpoint binding abstraction
A session may bind to endpoints such as:

- CLI / terminal
- Telegram DM / topic
- Discord channel / thread
- Slack channel / thread
- Teams conversation / thread
- webui / desktop workspace surface

This makes session continuity a core Hermes capability rather than a UI-only capability.

---

## Important scope note
This proposal is **not** asking for full remote PTY/shell streaming in v1.

The initial goal is **session continuity**, not literal terminal mirroring.

That means preserving:

- conversational context
- task continuity
- session identity
- resumability across surfaces

A more advanced terminal attachment model could come later.

---

## Adjacent idea: Projects
A related concept worth considering is **projects**.

A project could provide a higher-level container around sessions, with persistent project context such as:

- supporting documents
- notes
- linked files
- project-specific memory/context
- related sessions across surfaces

That would help with workflows where a user wants not just one portable session, but a persistent working context containing:

- multiple sessions
- reference docs
- maybe shared workspace state

In other words:

- **session** = one conversational/task thread
- **project** = a durable context that can retain supporting materials and multiple related sessions

This may be a separate feature track, but it seems highly complementary.

---

## Why gateway parity matters
If session continuity becomes strong in:

- hermes-webui
- AionUI
- hermes-desktop

but weak in:

- Telegram
- Discord
- Slack
- Teams

then Hermes will feel fragmented depending on interface.

The better long-term direction is:

> one session model, many surfaces

---

## Suggested first milestone
A practical first milestone would be:

1. expose session/endpoint binding info
2. support session resume across CLI + at least one gateway surface
3. make it obvious whether a session title is only a Hermes label or also tied to a native platform thread/topic

That alone would already be a major step forward.

---

## Question for maintainers
Is this already planned or partially implemented in current work on:

- webui
- desktop
- gateway/session architecture

If so, it would be useful to know whether the intended path is:

1. extend the current gateway model toward cross-surface session continuity, or
2. steer users toward webui/desktop as the primary solution for this workflow

---

## Short closing
The core proposal is simple:

> Hermes should let users start a session in one interface and continue it from another without losing the thread.

That feels like a high-value capability and aligned with where the product is already heading.
